text: A 41-year-old woman described right upper quadrant pain after a fatty meal last night. She recalled nausea and one episode of vomiting but no diarrhoea. Biliary colic arises when a gallstone transiently obstructs the cystic duct. Murphy sign positive with inspiratory arrest suggests acute cholecystitis rather than simple colic. On reflection, fatty-meal RUQ pain plus a positive Murphy sign should trigger ultrasound and surgical review.

provenance_note: Community pneumonia spans — disjoint from appendicitis anchors
text: Mr Lee is a 68-year-old with two days of productive cough and fever after a viral illness. He noticed rusty sputum this morning and felt breathless climbing stairs. Community-acquired pneumonia is typically a lower-respiratory infection acquired outside hospital. Focal crackles with raised CRP and a lobar infiltrate support a bacterial pneumonia working diagnosis. Therefore early antibiotics after cultures and a severity score remain standard when sepsis risk is present.
